pages.title: Emails and phone at work

situation.text: You write a short work email in English and prepare for a phone call. A colleague helps you with the opening, the request and the closing.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can open a work email, make a polite request, close it with thanks, and introduce yourself on the phone.
canDo: Open an email: I’m writing to…
Make a request: Could you send…?
Close: Thanks for your help. Best, …
Introduce yourself on the phone: This is Amy from…
success: I introduce myself on the phone.
pages.think: How do you start and end a work email in Portuguese? Do you use “Prezado” and “Atenciosamente”?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: escrever o primeiro e-mail de trabalho em inglês.
solo: Pergunte se o estudante escreve e-mails no trabalho e o que acha difícil.
Mostre os 4 critérios.
group: Cada estudante diz uma coisa que escreve por e-mail.
extra: Do you prefer email or phone?
How many emails do you write a day?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about communication at work.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: A simple job interview (last lesson): “I’m good at…”. Ask: What are you good at?

qs.q: Do you check email every day?

qs.pt: Qual é o seu endereço de e-mail?

pages.tip: Use the answers to practice saying “at” and “dot”.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma e levantar vocabulário de comunicação.
extra: Who do you write to most?
Do you use WhatsApp for work?

errors.r: My email is … at … dot com.
I send messages. / I send an email.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Work emails in English have a clear shape. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Hi Sam, (friendly) or Dear Ms. Lee, (more formal).
Best, · Thanks, · Best regards, — short and polite.
You say “This is Amy”, not “I am Amy”.

qs.q: How do you start a work email?
qs.pt: Como começar um e-mail de trabalho?

levels.A1: Hi Sam, or Dear Ms. Lee,
levels.A2: “Hi” for a friend, “Dear Ms. Lee” for a new contact.
levels.B1: Use Hi + first name with colleagues, and Dear + title + last name when it is formal or new.
levels.B2: Match the tone to the relationship: Hi Sam, for a colleague, Dear Ms. Lee, for a new or formal contact.

qs.q: How do you end a work email?
qs.pt: Como terminar um e-mail de trabalho?

levels.B1: Common endings are Best, Thanks, and Best regards, followed by your name.
levels.B2: Short closings such as Best, or Thanks, are common; Sincerely, is saved for very formal letters.

qs.q: How do you say your name on the phone?
qs.pt: Como dizer seu nome ao telefone?

levels.B1: You say “This is Amy” and then the company, and ask: “Can I speak to…?”
levels.B2: “Hello, this is Amy from Blue Sky; could I speak to Ms. Lee?” is a standard opening.

pages.compare: In Brazilian emails “Prezado(a)” and “Atenciosamente” are common. In English, “Hi” and “Best,” are often enough at work. What do you use in your company?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto: abertura e fecho de e-mails, e “This is…”.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com e-mails do estudante.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica.
extra: How formal are your emails?
What is a good subject line?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: compare tom e formalidade em e-mails no Brasil e nos EUA.

pass1.pt: O que a Amy está fazendo?

teach.goal: Compreender o essencial antes de ver o texto.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: o que a Amy faz.
2ª escuta: destinatária, pedido, prazo e fecho.
answers: Pass 2: Ms. Lee · invoice · Friday · Best
extra: Is the email formal? How do you know?
What does Amy plan to do next?

qs.q: What will Amy do if there is no reply?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.
starters: If there is no reply, she will…

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê a Amy; você lê o Max.
Peça que reconte.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
answers: A client, Ms. Lee · the invoice · by Friday · call her
extra: What would you write in the email?
Why does Max say “Now ask for what you need”?

errors.w: Could you send me the invoice until Friday?
errors.r: Could you send the invoice by Friday?

support: Mostre o PT depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Open an email and say your reason: I’m writing to ask about…
Make a polite request: Could you send the file?
Close an email or a call kindly.
Say your name on the phone.
A short, friendly closing before your name.
Ask for a person on the phone.

items.en: I’m writing to ask about the order.
This is Amy from Blue Sky.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks e descobrir a função.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?”.
Peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma ★ e explica.
answers: Opening · Request · Closing · Phone · Formal greeting
extra: Which one is for email only? Which for the phone?

swap.frame: I’m writing to {reason}. Could you send {thing} {when}?
swap.tpt: Estou escrevendo para {reason}. Você poderia enviar {thing} {when}?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Could you please send it at your earliest convenience?
My name is Amy and I work at Blue Sky.
I look forward to hearing from you.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões (I’m writing to… / Could you send…?). to + verbo base; Could + base.
solo: Mostre o padrão no diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.
extra: Make it shorter for a colleague: Can you send…?
Change the deadline.
support: Só I’m writing to… na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine: I’m writing to confirm. Could you send the file? Thanks for your help.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Put your tongue lightly between your teeth: Thanks /θ/. Portuguese speakers often say “t” or “s”: avoid “tanks” and “sanks”.

own.prompt: Write one sentence with “th” words: thanks, Thursday, think, three.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Did your tongue touch your teeth lightly?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: o som “th” /θ/ (thanks, Thursday, three).
solo: Mostre a língua entre os dentes no espelho.
Identify e depois uso próprio.

Se acertar rápido, peça outra versão formal.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — the phone call

brief.teacher: You are the client (Ms. Lee). Answer the phone and add a small problem.
brief.student: You are an employee: call, say who you are, ask for the file and close with thanks.

orders: Say who you are on the phone
Say why you are calling or writing
Ask the client to send something by a day
complications: The client cannot hear you well: repeat slowly.
The client is not available: leave a message.
You need to spell your email address.
The client asks you to send it again.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use empresa e nomes reais ou fictícios do estudante.
Rodada 1: chunks. Rodada 2: palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
extra: How do you leave a message?
stretch: Deixe uma mensagem de voz de 20 segundos.

pages.title: Group mission — email and call
pages.goal: Each group must write a short work email and make a phone call to follow up.

missions.mission: Write an email asking for a file. The client calls back.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m writing to…” and “Could you send…?”

missions.constraint: Use “This is… from…” and “Can I leave a message?”

missions.mission: Write a thank-you email after a meeting, then read it aloud.
missions.constraint: Use “Thanks for your help.” and a friendly closing.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: e-mail e telefone no mesmo contexto.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio → palavras-chave → sem roteiro.
answers: Modelo: “Dear Ms. Lee, I’m writing to ask about my order. Could you send the invoice by Friday? Thanks for your help. Best, Amy”
extra: Is your email too long?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short work email. Ask someone to send a document by a day. Use a clear opening and closing.
pages.model: Hi Sam, **I’m writing to** ask about the schedule. **Could you send** the new list by Thursday? **Thanks for your help.** Best, Amy
checklist: I used Hi / Dear and a name.
I closed with thanks and my name.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.

group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add a subject line.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Hi Sam, could you send the file? Thanks for your help.
I’m writing to ask about my order. Could you send the invoice by Friday?
ladder.goal: Give a reason and a deadline.

ladder.say: I’d appreciate it if you could send the invoice by Friday, as we need it for our records.
Should it be convenient, I’d be grateful if you could forward the invoice before the end of the week.
I would be most obliged if you could see your way to forwarding the invoice at your earliest convenience.
ladder.goal: Use refined formal register with tact.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
